items.title: what I want to do this week to shape the future of AI
Routing Quantum Data Without Ever Reading It
items.summary: In episode 1041 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Vijoy Pandey, SVP/GM Outshift by Cisco, the groundbreaking challenge of routing quantum data without ever reading it. Dr. Pandey explains how traditional store-and-forward networking principles are impossible in quantum networking, where information cannot be measured. He also describes Cisco's bet on horizontal scaling: connecting a hundred quantum computers of a thousand qubits each into one distributed system of a hundred thousand qubits, which only works if the network can switch quantum information without ever looking at it.

items.title: My AI Agent Bought Me A Car
items.summary: Sam Herring’s first real test of Hermes Agent was a shopping tool that matched clothes to photos of ancient pottery. A few months later, the same agent was checking government auction sites every day until it found him a retired three-wheel parking ticket car, which he now drives around San Francisco. In this episode, recorded at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America in San Jose, Sam, who works on the RL post-training team at Nous Research, goes from those everyday wins to the question everyone in AI is asking: can agents improve themselves? He explains how Hermes grew from an internal productivity tool into one of the most talked-about open-source agents, and why letting it write its own skills was the moment it clicked for users. He also describes an early version that could design its own RL environment, train on Thinking Machines’ Tinker, and hot-swap the new weights into a model running locally. Sam then breaks down Trace to Environment, an idea he credits to Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.6-Pro work, and the loop Nous is building around it: find the exact point where an agent fails, cluster those failures by type, synthesize environments that recreate them, and train on them again and again. The second half moves from training to inference. We get into whether reasoning models overthink, why leaning on pretraining knowledge can be a model’s Achilles heel, and why choosing a reasoning effort level may be a temporary quirk. Sam also makes his case for activation steering as an underexplored way to get more out of small models, explains where steering meets interpretability, and describes what true continual learning could look like. Demetrios Brinkmann: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dpbrinkm Sam Herring: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-herring-67225819a Timestamps: [0:00] Cold open [1:21] Meet Sam from Nous Research [2:39] How Hermes Agent started [3:38] From pottery to a parking ticket car [7:40] Benchmarking life admin tasks [8:58] Agents that write their own skills [10:10] RL at Nous a year ago [12:24] Hot swapping self-trained weights [15:00] Xiaomi and Trace to Environment [17:22] Turning agent failures into training [20:27] Where the RSI conversation is heading [21:34] Token efficiency and overthinking [26:30] Steering models at inference time [32:35] Toward true continual learning [34:54] Wrap up

items.title: Jensen Huang Admits He Was Unfaithful As Nvidia Board Opens An Independent Probe
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an affair following reports of a Chinese intelligence operation targeting the company. We analyze the security and financial implications of this scandal. Following reports that he was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation, Jensen Huang has issued a formal apology to his family and staff regarding his personal conduct. The board at Nvidia has initiated an independent probe into these espionage allegations, though current assessments indicate no compromise of US national security or proprietary trade secrets. This situation has drawn attention from Republican House committee chairs who have requested a closed-door briefing to evaluate the firm's security protocols. Market reaction has been swift, with Nvidia shares dropping 5.2 percent in pre-market trading, impacting the value of the Jensen and Lori Huang Living Trust. items.title: Blue Origin Gets NASA Moon Rover Delivery As Eight Firms Share Up To $10 Billion
items.summary: NASA has set a 10 billion dollar ceiling for lunar delivery contracts to scout for ice at the Moon south pole. We break down the logistics of this decade-long program. NASA is restructuring its approach to lunar exploration through the Commercial Lunar Payload Service program. This framework coordinates eight private providers to manage payload logistics, including the delivery of scientific instruments. The initiative focuses on identifying lunar resources, specifically water ice, which is essential for future mission sustainability and base construction. Blue Origin has been awarded a 94 million dollar contract to deliver the Promise rover, which will use nuclear power to operate in permanently shadowed regions. Meanwhile, SpaceX plans to support this infrastructure by deploying communication satellites in 2026. items.title: South Korea Proposes A $3.5 Billion Frontier AI Model Project In Its 2027 Budget
items.summary: South Korea is launching a massive frontier AI initiative to build competitive models and challenge global tech leaders by 2027. President Lee Jae-myung has proposed a record budget of 820.9 trillion won, with significant funding directed toward semiconductor advancement and domestic AI development. This strategy includes a 4.7 trillion won project to cultivate local talent and resources, aiming to establish a lead developer capable of matching international performance standards. We examine how this government-backed investment creates a roadmap for building a sovereign foundation model. Beyond software, the budget supports field trials for physical AI across eight sectors, including manufacturing and defense. By digitizing the expertise of experienced workers, the government plans to integrate advanced technology into real-world industrial applications. items.title: Cognizant Survey Finds 91% Of Indian Executives Yet To See AI Revenue Impact
items.summary: AI adoption in India is seeing rapid employee training, but enterprise revenue impact remains elusive. We analyze the latest data. A new study of 700 enterprise employees and 75 executives across 10 industries reveals a gap between AI adoption and bottom-line results. While 97 percent of employees report productivity gains, only 15 percent see average improvements, and executives have yet to record revenue impact or cost reduction. Our analysis breaks down these findings to explain why many firms are struggling to translate technology usage into financial performance. Beyond corporate metrics, the report highlights the potential for AI to add up to 84 billion dollars to the India GDP. With 74 percent of employees having completed formal training, the focus is shifting from simple implementation to achieving tangible business outcomes. items.title: How Quantum Teleportation Works on Messy New York Fiber (with Vijoy Pandey)
items.summary: In Episode #1041, Dr. Vijoy Pandey (SVP and General Manager of Outshift, Cisco's incubation engine) returns for a third visit to explain why multi-agent systems fail without anyone noticing. Agents from different vendors, clouds and organisations can now exchange perfectly valid messages, but connection is not cognition: they do not agree on what those messages mean. Vijoy's team analyzed multi-agent sessions from its own production deployments and from public traces, and found a cognitive failure in every single one. In this episode, he lays out the kinds of failure he sees and how fast they compound, introduces the open-source observability platform and protocols Outshift has shipped to catch and correct drift mid-task, details a record-breaking quantum network running on real New York City fiber, and explains why probabilistic AI software running on deterministic hardware is a mismatch worth fixing. Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1041
